title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 150
paragraphs: This is the Argives' own report about these matters. But another story is told in Greece, to the effect that Xerxes sent a herald to Argos before setting out to campaign against Greece. When this herald arrived, he said: “Men of Argos, King Xerxes says this to you: we hold that Perses, from whom we are descended, was the son of Perseus son of Danaë, born of Andromeda daughter of Cepheus; and by this account it would seem that we are descended from you. It is not fitting, then, that we should go on an expedition against those from whom we trace our descent, nor that you should set yourselves against us by helping others. Rather, it is fitting that you keep still and remain by yourselves; for if things turn out as I intend, I shall hold no people in higher honor than you.” On hearing this, the Argives, it is said, considered the matter a weighty one, and so at first they made no offer of help, nor did they ask for any share. But later, when the Greeks tried to bring them into the alliance, then — knowing well that the Lacedaemonians would not give them a share in the command — they asked for a share in command merely as a pretext for staying neutral.
